figures.finding: For 2026 IRPEF is 23% to €28,000, 33% from €28,000 to €50,000 (cut from 35% by the 2026 budget law) and 43% above; there is no tax-free band, but an employment-income credit (€1,955 up to €15,000 of income) reduces the tax; a regional surcharge (base 1.23%, each region may raise it by up to 2.1 points) and a municipal surcharge (up to 0.8%) apply on top.

regional.setBy: each region by its own law (D.Lgs. 68/2011 art. 6)

value.over200k: benefit of the 33% cut is neutralised above €200,000 of total income (L. 199/2025, art. 1, c. 3-4)

figures.finding: Workers in entertainment, employed or self-employed (including those with a partita IVA), are insured in INPS's Fondo Pensioni Lavoratori dello Spettacolo at 33% for pension (23.81% borne by the employer or client, 9.19% by the worker), and the employer or client pays the whole and withholds the worker's share; for those first insured after 1995 pay above the 2026 annual ceiling of €122,295 bears a 5% solidarity contribution (2.5/2.5) and a 0.50% worker contribution, while for those insured by 1995 a daily ceiling of €892 applies; the worker adds 1% on pay above €56,224 a year (€180 a day). Freelance work outside entertainment falls in the Gestione separata at 26.07% for a professional with no other scheme (25% pension + 0.72% + 0.35% ISCRO), on income up to €122,295 with a minimum base of €18,808.
